messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] WillowBank VPC Gateway (appgw-prod-us-east) — elevated websocket timeouts + client retry surge detected. Error mix: 502/504 + connection resets. Pager: SRE oncall. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/appgw-streaming-surge

Alice Chen: oncall ack, assigning. Paging eng-runtime and infra-oncall. I'll coordinate customer comms.

Marta Alvarez: From WillowBank: production traffic has ~30% streaming session drops after ~45s, their client lib retries aggressively every 2s which is amplifying load. They've labelled this P1. Please advise fast mitigations.

Ken Patel: looking at VPC egress and gateway logs now. Seeing repeated TLS close_notify from upstream origin during handshake which triggers our reconnect logic. Gateway worker threads show backlog and high accept-queue length.

Rohit Kumar: pulling runtime traces. Pattern: many short-lived reconnects (3-6s) from same tenant wb-231, causing accept storm -> queue saturation -> timeouts. We should short-circuit client retries with server-side throttling per-tenant + temporary 503 fallback to break retry loop.

Alice Chen: mitigation plan (immediate):
1) apply per-tenant handshake throttle for tenant id wb-231 (limit new WS handshakes to 5/s)
2) enable streaming backpressure mode on appgw (drop/reject new handshakes when worker busy)
3) set temporary 503 fallback on saturated workers so clients backoff
I will implement 1 & 3 now.

Rohit Kumar: i'll prepare runtime flag and config. Quick command I'm about to run: 
```bash
/ops set-tenant-rate --tenant wb-231 --handshake-rate 5 --reason "emergency handshake throttle"
/ops set-appgw-fallback --env prod --policy return_503_on_worker_saturation
```

Ken Patel: also increasing websocket proxy buffer and shortening idle keepalive to reduce stuck connections: will change worker_keepalive to 60s for appgw-prod-us-east.

Alice Chen: applying throttle and fallback now. Will monitor metrics (handshakes/s, ws_disconnect_rate, 5xx_rate).

WillowBank-ops: thanks, we've pushed the change to our client logs to spam less while you investigate — seeing fewer rapid reconnects already. Please confirm if you need us to push a client version change.

Rohit Kumar: throttle applied. Runtime returned OK. Snapshot of the config we pushed: 
```json
{"tenant":"wb-231","handshake_limit_per_sec":5,"fallback":"503_on_saturation","applied_by":"oncall"}
```

Alice Chen: metrics update +20m after mitigation: handshake rate for wb-231 down 4x, streaming disconnects down ~60%, worker accept-queue normalized. 5xx spikes reduced. Keeping mitigation for 30m, will not remove until stable and account agrees.

Lydia Park: noted reduction in customer impact. Recommend account team coordinate a planned client-side backoff release (exponential backoff with jitter) to prevent recurrence.

Marta Alvarez: I'll ask WillowBank for a small client patch to update retry policy and confirm schedule.

Jamal Singh: follow-up: we'll schedule permanent server-side safeguards: token-bucket per-tenant handshake limiter + circuit-breaker that returns Retry-After header to give clients deterministic backoff. I'll create RFC and link to this thread.

Rohit Kumar: quick note — we observed related TLS close_notify from origin; working with infra to investigate origin health and TLS renegotiation behavior. Might be contributing.

Alice Chen: customer notified and monitoring. Downgrading severity: P1 -> P2, but keeping this thread open for final remediation and postmortem notes. Great work. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status changed: P1 -> P2 by Alice Chen. Incident auto-note: mitigation applied at 3678904520, initial anomaly detected at 3678904321.

WillowBank-ops: Appreciative of the rapid help. We'll leave our ops channel open for any handoffs.

Alice Chen: leaving mitigation in place for 30m, will coordinate handoff to eng-sre for follow-up and postmortem. Closing active pager in 40m unless regression.

incident-bot: Incident status: monitoring. Closed active page at 3678905100. Refer to incident task #INC-2026-487 for postmortem and owner assignment.
